is_anopheles.evidence: Studies Anopheles funestus, described as 'one of the major malaria vectors in Africa' (Page 1, Abstract).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper performs genome-wide SNP discovery across 50 nuclear genes in Anopheles funestus, but does not genotype or report any of the specified target insecticide resistance markers (such as GSTe2 L119F, Cyp6p9a_R, Cyp6p9b_R, or Ace-1 N485I).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: No genotype or allele counts/frequencies for target resistance markers are reported.

african_field_population.evidence: Field specimens of An. funestus were collected from Kela village in Chikwawa district in southern Malawi (Page 8, Methods).

is_primary_study.evidence: Primary research article reporting original SNP identification and sequencing in An. funestus.

sub_country_location.evidence: Kela village in Chikwawa district, southern Malawi (Page 8).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: The exact collection year for the field samples from Malawi is not specified in the text.

duplicate_risk.evidence: Routine small-scale specimen collection (7 field mosquitoes and laboratory strains) for gene sequencing and SNP discovery.

supplement.evidence: Supplementary materials are not required as the paper does not examine target resistance markers.

assessment.summary: This study identifies 494 SNPs across 50 nuclear genes in Anopheles funestus by sequencing 21 specimens (7 field-caught mosquitoes from Malawi, 7 FUMOZ-R, and 7 FANG laboratory strain individuals). Although it evaluates genetic diversity and maps gene positions, it does not target or report genotype data for any defined target insecticide resistance markers.
exclusion_reasons: Does not report any target resistance markers (e.g. GSTe2 L119F, Cyp6p9a_R, Cyp6p9b_R, Ace-1 G280S/N485I).
Does not report extractable genotype or allele frequency data for target resistance markers.
